_meta.purpose: Source of truth for every reusable component in /components. An agent generating a new page must check this file first.
_meta.rule: If a page needs something not listed here, do NOT invent a new one-off component that duplicates an existing pattern. Instead, flag it as a "component gap": name the gap, describe what's needed, and point to the closest existing component it might extend. Record the gap in this file's "_gaps" array (add one if it doesn't exist yet) rather than silently building something ad hoc.
_meta.scope_note: This covers /components only. Page templates that compose several of these (e.g. CaseStudyPage) are included too, tagged category: "page_template", since a future agent needs to know they exist before building a competing template from scratch.
known_inconsistencies: Two near-identical blues in use: color.brand.accent (#004aeb, the 'real' token) and color.brand.highlight (#0658FC, used only on /explorations and the blog author box). Unresolved — see tokens.json.
Navbar and MobileMenu keep two separate hand-maintained nav link lists; MobileMenu imports navLinks from Navbar but styles its own links, so link states have to be changed in both.

Navbar.description: Sticky full-width top bar: logo, primary nav links (desktop only), mobile hamburger (MobileMenu). Rendered once, globally, in app/layout.tsx.
variants: none — singleton, rendered once for the whole site

states.default: Transparent background, at the top of an unscrolled page.
states.link:hover: text-white, a sharp-cornered (no radius) color.brand.accent background behind the label (-mx-1.5 -my-1 px-0.5 py-px, negative margins so the extra padding doesn't shift row spacing). Desktop links only. ShuffleText was tried here and removed — a scrambled run's advance width doesn't match the real label, so it visibly spilled past the tight hover background.
states.link:active_route: text-white (matches hover color) + aria-current="page", determined via usePathname().
states.link:disabled: href: null renders a static, non-interactive text-white/30 span instead of a Link.

Navbar.when_to_use: Never render directly on a page — it already lives in the root layout and appears on every route automatically.
do_not: Don't add a second Navbar instance on any page.

Don't add a nav link here without also deciding whether it belongs in MobileMenu's link list (they are currently separate, hand-maintained lists — About/Blog placeholders exist commented out in both).

LeftNav.description: Hero sidebar: heading, subheading, TrustedStrip, CtaButtons. Used on the homepage, /call, /explorations, and /clients, each passing its own heading/subheading copy.

variants.sticky: boolean prop. true = pinned to the viewport, height calc(100vh-6.5rem) (used with page-level scroll, e.g. homepage, /explorations). false (default) = fills a fixed-height row (used by /call, which has its own internal-scroll shell).
variants.balanceHero: boolean prop, applies text-balance/text-pretty for nicer line wrapping. Off by default because the homepage H1's line breaks were hand-tuned.
variants.headingSize: string prop, Tailwind class override for desktop heading size (default desk:text-[30px]).
variants.headingFontClassName: string prop, extra className applied only to the <h1> — e.g. a next/font className to swap the heading's font on a single page without touching the site-wide font-display.
variants.variant: default keeps the shared 405px sidebar and standard hero rhythm; clients uses the supplied Figma proportions: a responsive 431px desktop sidebar, 32px heading/description gap, 40px desktop heading, and 16px description.

states.entrance: fade-up animation on mount, staggered via inline animation-delay per child block.

LeftNav.when_to_use: Any page that needs the site's "hero sidebar" pattern: big heading + subheading + trusted-by strip + CTA buttons, paired with a content column to its right.
do_not: Don't confuse this with CaseSidebar — case study pages use a different, data-driven sidebar (client/year/involvement info) instead of this hero copy.
It renders as <aside>, not <nav> — it's hero copy + CTAs, not a navigation link list. Don't wrap it in nav semantics.
Don't hardcode a new hero block elsewhere — extend this component's props instead.

CaseSidebar.description: Case-study-specific sidebar: back button, ClientInfo (client/year/involvement/link), long-form description, CtaButtons. Sticky on desktop.
variants: none — always the same shape, data comes from the CaseStudy object

states.mobile: Renders nothing (client info moves under the title, description hidden) — see comment in file.

CaseSidebar.when_to_use: Case study pages only (components/case-study/CaseStudyPage.tsx), one per page, paired with a <main> content column as a sibling (not nested).
do_not: Don't give this a width of its own — it stays desk:w-[405px], matching the default LeftNav and blog asides. The approved /clients LeftNav variant is the only 431px exception.

Showcase.description: Renders the homepage's project list as the page's <main> landmark. One ProjectCard per project.

variants.scroll: "internal" (default) = column scrolls independently inside a fixed-height shell. "page" = no internal scroll, used on the homepage so the page itself scrolls and the footer can appear below the fold.

states: none — content is static per the projects data
tokens_used: spacing (gap-8 / 32px between cards on mobile, gap-6 / 24px from desk up)
Showcase.when_to_use: Homepage only, currently — it IS the page's <main>, not a generic reusable list container.
do_not: Don't render more than one per page (it's a <main> landmark).
Don't reuse this for a different image set (e.g. explorations) — that page has its own ExplorationGallery instead.

Don't lower the mobile gap toward ProjectCard's 12px media-to-info gap. It was 16px against that 12px and the column read as one undifferentiated stack — no card boundary was perceptible. The between-card gap has to stay clearly the largest vertical space in the column. Mobile being larger than desktop here is deliberate, not an oversight: mobile stacks the info into three lines, desktop keeps it to one row.

ProjectCard.description: One homepage project entry: media (image or video), optional overlay logo, and an info row 12px below the media (client name + one-line tagline on the left, uppercase services + year on the right). Links out (internal Link or external <a>) — the info row sits inside the link, so hovering the text also drives the media zoom.
variants: external vs internal link, driven by project.external

info row: desktop (>= desk) = single 50px space-between row, bottom-aligned, per Figma 'Frame 2147243671'. Below desk = the two groups stack, meta keeps its own space-between so the year holds the right edge.

services list: truncates to one line at >= desk; below desk it wraps instead (a 3-discipline list needs ~307px vs the 296px a 375px card offers). Each discipline is a nowrap span so breaks land on separators only.
info row renders nothing at all when a project has no tagline/services/year

states.hover: Media scales up 1.05x via group-hover, clipped by the frame. Info row is opacity-80 at rest, opacity-100 on its own :hover (not group-hover — only fires when the pointer is directly over the text block, independent of the media zoom).
states.entrance: fade-up with a staggered delay based on list index (capped at 800ms). The info row inherits the card's animation rather than having its own.

tokens_used: radius: none (square corners are intentional, not an oversight)
spacing (gap-3 media-to-info, gap-3 stacked info on mobile, gap-4/gap-8 within the desktop row)
typography.font.mono (Geist Mono 500, via the font-mono utility) on the services/year meta row
ProjectCard.when_to_use: Inside Showcase only, one per project.
do_not: Don't add border-radius/shadow — square corners are a deliberate Figma decision.
Don't skip the priority/fetchPriority wiring on the first card — it's the homepage's LCP element.
Don't pin the info row to a fixed 50px height — it's intrinsic (24px title at 1.2 + 16px tagline at 1.3 = 49.6px) so a wrapping mobile tagline can't clip.
Don't let a tagline run long on a project with three disciplines — the wider meta column leaves it only ~46 characters before it truncates at 1200px.
Don't write funding or valuation claims into project.tagline that aren't sourced — see the copy-review note in lib/projects.ts.

CtaButtons.description: The paired 'Chat on Telegram' + 'Start a Conversation' buttons.

variants.telegramSolidBlack: boolean prop. false (default) = translucent color.neutral.button-dark with a hover lighten (used in LeftNav/CaseSidebar). true = solid black, no hover lighten (used in Footer).

CtaButtons.when_to_use: Anywhere the site's two primary CTAs need to appear together (currently: LeftNav, CaseSidebar, Footer).
do_not: Don't change 'Start a Conversation' back into an internal <Link> to /call — it deliberately opens links.discoveryCall (an external Cal.com URL) in a new tab now.
Don't add a third button here — it's built for exactly two, laid out with flex-1 each.

LeadCallout.description: Accent-blue objection callout with a 3px left rule, sitting directly above TrustedStrip in the hero sidebar.
variants: none — responsive only: 12px type throughout, in 10px of padding on mobile and 12px from the desk breakpoint up
states: static — the fade-up entrance comes from the LeftNav wrapper, not this component
tokens_used: color.brand.accent (fill at 20%, left rule at full)
LeadCallout.when_to_use: In every sidebar: LeftNav, BlogSidebar, BlogPostSidebar and CaseSidebar. It raises the objection the trusted-by logos answer, so it belongs immediately above TrustedStrip — or directly above CtaButtons in CaseSidebar, which has no strip.
do_not: Don't pin it to a fixed height — padding plus a single 12px/120% line already produces it, and hardcoding it clips the second line at the widths where the copy wraps.
Don't pass the copy in from the call site — it's self-contained like TrustedStrip, so there's exactly one place to edit the line.

TrustedStrip.description: "Trusted by top YC companies" label + an infinite horizontal marquee of logos (baked strip image + a few extra SVG logos), duplicated once for a seamless loop.
variants: none
states: continuous CSS marquee animation, no interactive states
do_not: Don't add a logo to only one of the two duplicated blocks — both copies must stay identical or the loop will visibly jump.
The first copy carries real alt text; the duplicate is aria-hidden — keep that split when adding logos.

MobileMenu.description: Hamburger button + dropdown panel containing the primary navigation links, mobile only.
variants: none

states.open: X icon, panel visible below the navbar, plus a color.neutral.scrim overlay (fixed, below the panel's z-index) that dims the rest of the page — the page bg is already pure black so a scrim, not a darker solid, is what makes the open state read as darker.

do_not: Don't remove desk:hidden — this is the mobile-only counterpart to Navbar's desktop nav links.
It imports Navbar's navLinks array, so add or remove primary destinations there.

Logo.description: Site wordmark (single SVG, mark + wordmark), links to /.
variants: none
do_not: Don't change the -ml-[4.7px] negative margin without re-checking the SVG's baked-in left whitespace — it's a deliberate optical alignment fix, not arbitrary.

Footer.description: Site footer: four columns (brand/copyright, Quick Links, Case Studies, newsletter blurb + NewsletterForm) over a full-width Union wordmark row.
Footer.status: Live. Rendered on app/page.tsx, app/blog/page.tsx, app/explorations/page.tsx, app/call/page.tsx, blog/BlogPostPage.tsx and case-study/CaseStudyPage.tsx.
variants: none

states.link:hover: The ShuffleText scramble on the label, and nothing else — the old hover:opacity-70 dim was removed when the shuffle went in. Every link is w-fit so its box hugs its text, which keeps the click target and the shuffle's hover target identical.

Footer.when_to_use: Once per page, as the very last element, on pages that scroll to a natural end.
do_not: Don't re-enable it without checking the background-image blur/z-index fix made for it earlier (Footer needed position: relative so it paints correctly above the page's background-image layers).
Its own <footer> requires relative positioning to stack correctly above absolutely-positioned page background layers — don't remove that.

variants: Display column is hidden on mobile (desk:flex only) — only Filter shows there.
ArticleFilters.when_to_use: Top of /blog only, currently a visual/interactive placeholder — it doesn't yet actually filter the article list below it.
do_not: Don't add a flex `gap` between the two columns without removing their percentage widths (or vice versa) — gap + width summing to 100% overflows the row. Use flex-1 if a gap is needed, matching the fix already applied here.

BlogImage.description: Shared Next Image adapter for the temporary local blog-image fallback and Sanity image assets, including hotspot crops and LQIP placeholders.
variants: fill for fixed card frames
intrinsic width and height for article heroes
states: Sanity blur placeholder when LQIP metadata exists
BlogImage.when_to_use: For blog index cards, article heroes, and related-article cards. It keeps image behavior identical while the CMS source is switched.
do_not: Don't build Sanity CDN URLs directly in page components; pass the normalized BlogImage value here.
Don't omit the sizes prop when using fill, because Next Image needs it for correct responsive selection.

ExplorationGallery.description: Renders the /explorations image list (full-width and 50/50-pair blocks) plus the Grid/Zoom toggle, plus a click-to-expand lightbox (framer-motion fade/scale, backdrop blur, prev/next arrows, Escape/arrow-key nav, body scroll lock).
variants: blocks prop: { kind: "full", src } | { kind: "pair", srcs: [a, b] }, ordered top-to-bottom exactly as rendered.

states.view:grid: Default. Derived (not separately tracked) from whether the lightbox is closed.
states.view:zoom: Derived from the lightbox being open — clicking 'Zoom' opens it at image index 0; closing the lightbox by any means reverts to 'grid'.
states.lightbox:open/closed: AnimatePresence-driven fade/scale; body overflow locked while open.

do_not: Don't reintroduce a separate `view` state — it's intentionally derived from openIndex so the active button can never desync from the actual lightbox state.
Don't give two side-by-side pair images `w-1/2` plus a `gap` together — same overflow bug as ArticleFilters; use `min-w-0 flex-1` instead.

SectionShell.description: Case study Q&A section wrapper: uppercase heading in the left half, full-width hairline rule, content in the right half (aligned to the vertical center rule).

variants.topRule: boolean. Adds a full-width hairline above the section (used for the FAQ block).
variants.headingSize: default keeps the 48px desktop heading; compact uses 32px and small uses 24px for longer headings that must stay within two lines.

SectionShell.when_to_use: Case study pages only, for the repeated 'heading left / content right' Q&A pattern (including the FAQ block).
do_not: Don't reuse this for a full-width section — it hardcodes a 50/50 desktop split matched to the case study sidebar layout. The blog page's FAQ section deliberately does NOT use this for exactly that reason; it builds its own full-width heading + content stack instead.

CaseFaq.description: FAQ accordion, one item open at a time (first open by default). Each question is an <h3> wrapping the toggle button.
variants: none — items prop drives content (FaqItem[])

states.item:open: Answer expanded via grid-template-rows animation, opacity 1.
states.item:closed: grid-rows-[0fr], opacity 0, but stays in the DOM (not unmounted).

CaseFaq.when_to_use: Case study pages (via SectionShell) and the /blog page (standalone, full width) — same shared FAQ content (lib/case-studies.ts pixelupFaq) and matching FAQPage JSON-LD schema on both.
do_not: Don't put the heading (<h3>) inside the <button> — headings cannot legally nest inside button elements. It wraps the button instead.

CaseMedia.description: CaseMediaSlot (single image/video frame with tone placeholder fills) + CaseMediaBlock ("full" 1160x696 frame or "pair" of 576x548 frames). Full and pair blocks can opt into a landscape 16:9 aspect for supplied wide showcase assets.

variants.tone: "white" | "faint" | "green" — placeholder fill shown when a slot has no real media yet.
variants.full aspect: standard keeps the approved 1160/696 crop; wide uses 16:9 at full width.
variants.pair aspect: standard keeps the approved 576/548 crop; wide uses 16:9 without changing the pair spacing or responsive stack.

states: priority prop: true = loading="eager" + fetchPriority="high" (the case hero image only); false = lazy.
CaseMedia.when_to_use: Case study pages only, between Q&A sections and as the hero.
do_not: Don't use the deprecated next/image `priority` prop on new usages here — this project is on Next 16, where it no longer implies fetchPriority="high"; use loading + fetchPriority explicitly instead.

CaseSection.description: Renders a CaseStudy section's lead paragraph, focus list, results rows, paragraphs, and/or numbered shipped-work list inside a SectionShell.
variants: content is conditional on which optional fields (lead/focus/results/paragraphs/bullets) exist on the section data
CaseSection.when_to_use: Case study pages only, once per CaseSection entry in a CaseStudy's sections array.
do_not: Don't add a new section shape without extending the shared CaseSection type in lib/case-studies.ts first.

ClientInfo.description: Client / Year / Involvement / optional Funding / Link rows with hairline dividers. Lives in CaseSidebar on desktop, under the title on mobile. One or more external links may share the final row.
variants: funding row renders only when supplied
single link uses the label Link; multiple links use Links and stack vertically

MoreProjects.description: "More Projects" section at the end of a case study: two equal-width project cards with an overlay logo/title/tags.
variants: none — refs prop (MoreProjectRef[]) drives which projects show

states.card:hover: Media scales up, same treatment as the homepage ProjectCard.

MoreProjects.when_to_use: End of every case study page.
do_not: Don't give the two cards a flex `gap` together with fixed widths that already sum to 100% — use flex-1, same fix as ArticleFilters/ExplorationGallery.

CaseStudyPage.description: Full case study page template: CaseSidebar + main content column (title, hero, optional opening media, CaseSection/CaseMedia loop, optional closing statement with follow-on media, CaseFaq, MoreProjects, Footer).
variants: study prop (CaseStudy) drives all content; draft studies remain directly previewable but are noindex and excluded from the sitemap
CaseStudyPage.when_to_use: Rendered once by app/case-studies/[slug]/page.tsx per case study. Also renders the FAQPage JSON-LD schema.
do_not: Don't build a competing case-study template — add a new CaseStudy entry to lib/case-studies.ts instead; this template handles layout for all of them.

ShuffleText.description: A text label that scrambles itself on hover: the whole label churns for 150ms, then resolves left to right over 330ms (480ms total). Wraps a link's label; the link keeps all of its own styling and ShuffleText only owns the animation.
variants: none — props are text (the label) and an optional className on the outer inline-block box

states.hover: 16 ticks at 30ms. The first frame fires synchronously on pointer-enter; HOLD_TICKS (5) hold the whole label in scramble, then RESOLVE_TICKS (11) resolve it left to right. Tick counts are fixed, not per-character, so a long label and a short one finish together.
states.reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce skips the animation entirely — the label just stays at rest.

ShuffleText.tuning: TICK_MS / HOLD_TICKS / RESOLVE_TICKS at the top of the file are the only knobs. Don't drop HOLD_TICKS to 0: resolving across the whole run locks the leading characters to their real letters within a frame or two, which is below what the eye registers, and the label then looks like it started already half-solved.
tokens_used: none — inherits font, size and color from the link that wraps it
ShuffleText.when_to_use: Nav and footer text link labels. Not currently used anywhere — pulled from Navbar's desktop primary nav and all four Footer link groups (Quick Links, Case Studies, Careers, Testimonials) because a scrambled run's advance width doesn't match the real label, which read as the text spilling out of Navbar's tight hover background. Component kept in case it's revisited with a fix (e.g. clipping the overlay to the locked width).
do_not: Don't use it on buttons or CTAs — those have their own bg/brightness hover states, and scrambling a call to action hurts legibility at the moment of decision.
Don't remove the invisible width-lock span: the random glyphs have different advance widths from the real ones, so without it every tick reflows the nav row and the footer columns.
Don't put it on a link whose box is wider than its text without adding w-fit to that link — the hover handlers sit on the text box, so the shuffle would only fire over part of the click target.
Don't wire it to :focus-visible — a keyboard user would get a churning label at the moment they're trying to read it.

CalEmbed.description: Inline Cal.com booking widget (@calcom/embed-react), dark-themed to match the site.
variants: none
states: none — Cal's own UI handles booking states internally
do_not: Don't change calLink/namespace without updating the matching getCalApi namespace call — they must match.

ClientRoster.description: The /clients page column labels and ordered list of ClientRow entries. The page-level heading stays exclusively in the sidebar. Desktop restores the three-column roster from the supplied reference: Client, Niche, and What we did, using a 1.6fr / 0.6fr / 0.8fr ratio so the logo column is the largest. The roster remains inset by 24px horizontally and 28px vertically, with 24px gaps between columns.
variants: none — the clients prop supplies the ordered roster
do_not: Don't reuse Showcase or ProjectCard for the roster — those components are media-led portfolio entries, while this is an information-led client archive.

ClientRow.description: One hairline-separated client entry with 25px top padding and 40px bottom padding at every viewport. Desktop uses three aligned columns: the dominant logo column, Niche, and What we did. Both text columns render at 60% white opacity. Mobile stacks the same content, preserves the approved 10px logo-to-niche gap, and keeps explicit Niche and What we did labels. Approved vectors render pure white inside optically audited contain frames, preserving their original aspect ratios without transform scaling. Vertera Health and Conigma are intentional color exceptions. Vertera preserves its white wordmark and outer icon with black petals against the white icon background. Conigma preserves its original wordmark shape in white, with a white rounded icon tile and black inner star. The default frame remains 134.4px by 24px. Per-logo width changes are applied to the rendered mark—not merely to unused frame space—by pairing each requested width with a sufficient proportional height in logoFrameClassBySlug. The current optical adjustments cover Autumn Pricing, Bland, CTGT, Conigma, Conscious Engines, DayFlow, Greptile, Henrylabs, Lasting Learn, My Wonder, NFA, Pogo, Reducto, Revyl, Sainapse, Streamline, Sully, Synthio Labs, Umbra, Vertera Health, Zenact, and Jumbo. Grovio currently uses the established accessible duplicated-logo placeholder because its SVG was not included. The final three engagement words stay together to prevent widow lines. The full client name remains in accessibility text and structured data rather than appearing beside the logo.
variants: approved logo vs duplicated-logo placeholder
ClientRow.when_to_use: Inside ClientRoster only, driven by lib/clients.ts.
do_not: Don't substitute a different company's logo for Grovio as if it were approved; replace its accessible placeholder when the real SVG arrives.
Don't replace the width variants with transform scaling; width-only sizing preserves the requested 24px height and 10px gap.
Don't apply the pure-white filter to Vertera Health or Conigma because it removes the contrast inside their icon marks.
Don't remove the shared contain frame, pure-white treatment for the other logos, or per-logo width adjustments without rechecking every supplied logo together.
Don't remove the final three-word nowrap group without rechecking the roster for one- or two-word widow lines.
